§5.2 · C70 §5.4/§5.5). Pinned at the FIRST HONEST READING, 2026-08-13.
FIRST READING: 10 dependency indexes established (7 discovered from source by
class-name shape, 10 declared by appendix 0B §3, unioned). ONE can refuse —
DependencyResolver.getAffected's AffectedSet discriminated union. The other
NINE are the rows below.
This reproduces C78 §0.h — 'nine indexes exist; exactly one can refuse' —
INDEPENDENTLY, from source rather than from the appendix's prose. The
denominator differs by one because 0B §3's own table lists TEN rows under a
sentence that says nine; the gate counts what it establishes and prints both
numbers, per C78 §0.2 (never restate a measured count as if it were stable).
NOTE ON SlabDependencyTracker. 0B §3 marks it '✓ via
DegradeSlabSketchCommand.canExecute()'. Measured at SlabDependencyTracker.ts:180-187,
that path console.warn()s and `return`s — the caller receives NOTHING it can
branch on, and no value distinguishes 'nothing depends on this' from 'I could
not determine'. It is a LOG, not a refusal. The gate's reading supersedes the
appendix tick per C78 §0.2, and this is the ledger's single most consequential
disagreement with its own source document.
EXIT CONDITION (C78 §20, U-INV-7 row): 'the measured 1-of-9 refusing indexes
reaches all' — i.e. cannotRefuse reaches EMPTY. A row leaves this list in the
same commit that gives that index a determination shape; a row that is no
longer measured but still listed is STALE and exits 3 (C70 §5.4). The list may
never grow: an index measured unable to refuse and NOT listed here is an
unledgered finding and also exits 3.
Every row is `<IndexName>/no-typed-refusal` — ARM B and ARM C are two readings
of one question and produce ONE finding per index, never two.
─── 2026-08-16 · lane G2 (A.12) · 9 rows → 8. ONE ROW STRUCK, PAID. ────────
DoorDependencyTracker/no-typed-refusal LEAVES this ledger. It is not
re-anchored and it is not excused: the index now carries a typed refusal path
and the gate measures it as `UNDETERMINED reason member`, `kind:'undetermined'`.
The row was PAID in an earlier commit and never struck, which is the exact
shape C78 §20's both-directions check exists to catch — and it caught it,
exiting 3 STALE LEDGER rather than passing over its own paid debt. Struck
here, in the commit that re-measures it (§7B.4: the pin moves in the commit
that pays it; a stale row is an uncommitted payment).
THE DENOMINATOR DID NOT MOVE THE OTHER WAY. The same run reported three
UNLEDGERED subjects — CeilingHostDependencyTracker, FloorHostDependencyTracker,
RoofDependencyTracker. NONE was added to this list, because all three were
measured to be FALSE POSITIVES of the gate's own analyser, not new debt:
the first two are constructor-only subclasses of a base this gate itself
scores as able to refuse, and the third refuses with `ENGINE_NOT_AVAILABLE`,
a C78 §8.1 union member the gate's hand-copied vocabulary had omitted. The
instrument was fixed; this ledger was NOT grown. Growing it would have
recorded three defects that do not exist and backdated a decision nobody made.

cannotRefuse.why: plugins/annotations/src/subsystem/AnnotationDependencyGraph.ts — annotation → host index, queryable both ways, no determination shape anywhere in the file. 'This element hosts no annotations' and 'I have no entry for this element' are the same value, so a delete cannot tell whether annotations are about to be orphaned.

packages/geometry-slab/src/floor/FloorSlabBindingHandler.ts:65 — slabId → floors, queryable. hostSlabId is one of only TWO dependency-naming fields C78 §0.g measures as HONOURED, and the index that honours it still cannot say 'I could not determine'.

apps/editor/src/engine/WallRebuildCoordinator.ts:183 — wallId ↔ wallId, reactive, re-emitted per flush. A flush that produced no junctions and a flush that never ran are indistinguishable to every consumer downstream of it.

packages/core-app-model/src/stores/LightingStore.ts:52 — roomId → lights, queryable, and 0B §3 records that NOTHING SUBSCRIBES. An unsubscribed index that also cannot refuse answers a question nobody asks with a value nobody could trust.

packages/geometry-slab/src/SlabDependencyTracker.ts:49,180-187 — wallId → Set<slabId>, reactive only (`graph` is private, no public getter). 0B §3 marks this '✓ can refuse via DegradeSlabSketchCommand.canExecute()'; measured, that branch console.warn()s and returns void. A log is not a refusal and no caller can branch on it — see the NOTE above.

packages/geometry-slab/src/SlabWallConnectivityService.ts:125,144,150 — slab ↔ wall connectivity, reactive. C78 §20's U-INV-14 row separately names :337 of this same file as a direct-write observer, so it both mutates outside the plan and cannot refuse.

packages/core-app-model/src/views/ViewDependencyTracker.ts:371,472,569,640 — levelId → viewIds and viewId → dirty elementIds. 0B §3 states the distinction precisely: it has SUPPRESSION and a GENERATION HOLD, which are not refusals — a held generation and an empty dirty set print the same value, so a view can be left unprojected with no record that it was ever asked.

packages/geometry-window/src/WindowDependencyTracker.ts:42,148 — getWindowIdsForWall(wallId): string[]. Same shape and same defect as the door tracker; the two are the hosted-element pair C15 governs.
